newsitem.title: FRANCE: IBCA keeps Paribas rating, SocGen on watch.
newsitem.headline: IBCA keeps Paribas rating, SocGen on watch.

text.p: European ratings agency IBCA said on Thursday it had confirmed its A1 and A ratings of French holding company Paribas but put an AA rating of Societe Generale on creditwatch with negative implications.
IBCA issued the ratings notice in a statement following news earlier in the day that Paribas was in talks on a speedy sale of Credit du Nord bank to Societe Generale for 2.2 billion francs.
IBCA said its A2 and A- ratings of Credit du Nord were on creditwatch with positive implications.
"The divestment by Cie Financiere de Paribas from Credit du Nord has been carried out in line with a strategy of focusing on its core investment banking business," the statement said.
"This deal bolsters the group's capitalisation...but will not have any significant impact on recurring profitability," it added.

It said that Credit du Nord's business and results were improving since the start of a serious restructuring plan in 1995 but that profitability remained weak, notably because of high structural costs compared to income.

IBCA said that Societe Generale was among one of the world's 20 biggest banks and that, even if its profitability and equity funds were relatively weaker than its U.S. and British rivals, the bank was a healthy one.

"Taking control of Credit du Nord is in line with a strategy of strengthening its retail banking business in France, where its know-how allows it to achieve satisfactory profitability," said the statement.
